title: Vaudeville acts and silent-film piano at the theater
summary: She stayed about a year at the theater, remembers singers who came through, played solo piano for silent movies, and the theater's location and demise are discussed.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, it's certainly the same type of music in some ways, as long as you know the chords. That's it. So you can play any of them. Are there any other bands or other jobs that you can think of, like you mentioned, like after that movie job? How long were you there? Or the theater job? That was with vaudeville, too.
Vaudeville. I must have been there about a year.
Did they have any other acts, like famous singers or artists that would come in from our town, if you can remember at that time?
I can remember some. I remember Dad James. I don't know if you can think about him. I don't remember. He was a good singer. And Luke Cannon.

We collect records. Of course, I've always collected records for 20 or 30 years now. And I have a lot of the old time records, too. The period of Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey and everyone of that kind. Oh, yes. So unless a person recorded, I wouldn't know a lot of those names.
Well, now, I wouldn't really know if they recorded those things or not. But they were in, they were standards. They stayed at the show. Other acts came, but they stayed.
You had to play for the silent movies?
Yeah, I played for both. I played for the silent movies.
Did the whole orchestra play? No, no, no.
Just the piano. That's where they used to be when I drove. Just the piano.
And then, I think they had four of Baudrill's Day.
Which side of the street? Is that the lake or riverside? I don't remember.
Is that about, is that very near the Astoria Hotel?
It could be somewhere around there. I just remember some third black. I think it was destroyed.

Must have been torn down. Pelican was in there, too, and the restaurant, the famous restaurant. They had music there, too. Yeah. For a long time. But that whole part of town is going now since they had the new... It is, it is, yeah. The Civic Center and all the city hall and everything along in there. Is there anything else about your life that, uh, music and the musicians that you heard and played with that you could add? For instance, were there any other outstanding pianists? Everyone knows Professor Minette, of course, is a great pianist. But were there any others that you remember hearing and watching when you were young and learning?
